summary: Initial discovery focused on Ventus's need for semantic reranking on top of an existing keyword search. Key constraints: sub-100ms p50 latency for rerank at 200 qps, compatibility with current Milvus cluster, preference for hosted first with option to go Dedicated or Private for data residency and KMS. Next steps agreed: pricing, benchmark guide, pilot with sample data, and security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (Ventus - Head of Search), Liam Chen (Ventus - Sr ML Eng), Priya Nair (Ventus - CTO)

00:00 Jamie Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we can see people popping in, I'm Jamie from Redwood inference, AE on this account, with Samir our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Maya Rodriguez: Hey Jamie, good thanks, Maya here. Sorry running a bit behind.
00:09 Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya - quick intro.
00:11 Jamie Park: No worries. Quick agenda - high-level goals, current stack, constraints, then dig into rerank and embeddings and how you'd like to integrate with your vector DB, then next steps.
00:20 Maya Rodriguez: Sounds good. Our main ask: we currently do textual search for our docs portal (Lucene based), want to add semantic reranking so top-20 results get reranked by relevance. Target is about 200 qps peak, p50 latency for the rerank stage should be under 100ms ideally. Also need data residency in EU but for the proof-of-concept we can do hosted.
00:36 Samir Patel: Great, thanks. Quick clarifying - when you say rerank is that full re-score of top K (e.g., top 20) or are you doing a fusion model / hybrid scoring?
00:44 Liam Chen: We're planning to score top 20 with embeddings-based similarity and combine that with our BM25 score - so hybrid. The embeddings part is a rerank that adds vector similarity scores.
00:52 Jamie Park: Got it. What's your current vector DB? You mentioned Lucene for keyword, are you running Milvus or something else for vectors?
00:58 Maya Rodriguez: We spun up Milvus last quarter for a few experiments. It's currently on-prem in our Frankfurt cluster. For the POC we'd be open to shipping a small sample dataset to a hosted service, but longer term we may want Dedicated or Private with VPC.
01:10 Samir Patel: Ok, good context. For throughput - is 200 qps the combined end-to-end search + rerank, or just the rerank stage?
01:17 Liam Chen: That's total queries hitting the search API; rerank will only be triggered for user queries where the top-K are fetched - effectively most queries, so plan for 200 qps rerank.
01:26 Samir Patel: Understood. In that case, two knobs matter on our side: embedding model/dimensionality (affects compute and index size) and batching/async rerank versus synchronous per-request.
01:36 Maya Rodriguez: We tried OpenAI's embeddings for a small test - 1536 dims - quality was good but the cost and index size spiked. Curious about smaller dims, like 768, tradeoffs?
01:46 Samir Patel: Right. 1536 (e.g., text-embedding-ada-002 style) gives better semantic separation in many domains, but 768 can be sufficient depending on corpus complexity. From an infra perspective, 768 reduces index size ~half and speeds up kNN. On Redwood Dedicated you can also use quantized models which reduce memory and improve throughput.
01:58 Jamie Park: Also want to flag that our hosting offers model choices and we can export embeddings to your Milvus; we support integrations with Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus out-of-the-box. For Private deployments we provide an agent to sync vectors into your existing cluster if you want to keep control.
02:12 Priya Nair: Security-wise we'll need SOC2 + KMS support, and the ability to control retention. For POC we can accept hosted but we need the option to move to VPC or on-prem later.
02:22 Jamie Park: Absolutely. We have SOC2, can provide our security pack, and Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and private control plane. We'll send the SOC2 and SOC2 type II evidence docs after the call.
02:33 Maya Rodriguez: Cool. On the reranker model - does Redwood host rerank models or do we bring our own? We have a small in-house model we could use, but open to Redwood endpoints.
02:43 Samir Patel: Both are supported. You can run hosted models (we provide a model catalog), bring-your-own container for Private or Dedicated, or use an endpoint that proxies to your existing model. For the latency numbers you mentioned, we often use a lightweight bi-encoder for similarity (fast) then an optional cross-encoder for high precision on a smaller K. Cross-encoder for top 5 only, for example.
02:59 Liam Chen: If we do bi-encoder for full 20 and cross-encoder for top 5, what's throughput look like?
03:05 Samir Patel: Roughly, bi-encoder is an embedding dot-product step - that's mostly vector ops and index lookup; with optimized GPU kernels and batching you can do thousands of similarity ops per GPU. The cross-encoder is the expensive part: if we run cross-encoder on top 5 at 200 qps, that's equivalent to 1000 inferences per second for the cross-encoder. For that we'd either need Dedicated capacity or scale hosted layers.
03:22 Maya Rodriguez: Hmm, 1000/sec cross-encoder seems heavy. We were hoping to keep cost modest.
03:27 Jamie Park: Tradeoffs: smaller cross-encoder, quantization, and running cross-encoder on CPU for small batches are options. Another common approach is to only run cross-encoder on queries flagged as low-confidence by the bi-encoder fusion. That reduces cross-encoder load significantly.
03:43 Priya Nair: How about vector dimensionality impact on Milvus? Our Milvus cluster is provisioned for 1536 dims currently. Would switching to 768 force reindex?
03:52 Liam Chen: We can reindex but that is painful at scale.
03:55 Samir Patel: Yes reindex required. If you plan to switch dims we'd recommend doing it in the POC on a sample index and measure. Also, Redwood can produce both 1536 and 768 embeddings so you can A/B offline before migrating.
04:09 Maya Rodriguez: Ok good. On indexing type - ANN vs exact? We're using IVF + HNSW in Milvus. Any suggestions?
04:16 Samir Patel: IVF+HNSW is reasonable for large corpora. For sub-10M vectors latency targets, HNSW parameters tuned for efSearch give good p50/p95. We'll share recommended Milvus tuning defaults in the benchmark guide.
04:28 Jamie Park: Also we'll include sample index configs that reached sub-100ms p50 for rerank workflows in similar customers.
04:33 Maya Rodriguez: Great. Question on hybrid scoring: how do you combine BM25 and cosine distances? We want a stable function and explainability.
04:41 Samir Patel: We typically normalize scores - z-score BM25 and cosine similarity transformed via logistic function - then a weighted linear combination. For explainability we keep the raw components in the response and provide weights. Also we support rerank policies where you can tune weights per route.
04:55 Liam Chen: That would be useful. Will need to test weighting heuristics.
04:58 Jamie Park: On integration, do you prefer Redwood to host embeddings generation and indexing, or do you want us to write to your Milvus?
05:06 Maya Rodriguez: For POC, we'll prefer Redwood-hosted to move quickly, but long term it's likely we'll keep vectors on-prem in Milvus for residency. How hard is switching from hosted to private later?
05:16 Samir Patel: It's supported - we can export embeddings and metadata, and we have a sync agent for private clusters. For Dedicated you get reserved capacity and a managed index in our infra, and for Private we can ship a control plane and sync pipeline. We recommend designing the pipeline to be storage-agnostic (i.e., write embeddings to an object store + index separately) to ease migrations.
05:33 Priya Nair: What about encryption at rest and KMS?
05:36 Jamie Park: For hosted, we manage encryption and can use customer-managed keys in Dedicated or Private. Private supports bringing your own KMS or HSM. We'll attach the security doc.
05:44 Maya Rodriguez: On metrics and observability - we need per-model latency, token-level cost, and tracing to tie back to our logs.
05:51 Samir Patel: Redwood Console provides per-route/per-model dashboards, token or operation-level cost breakdown, and request tracing. We can push traces to your telemetry via OTLP if you'd like.
06:02 Liam Chen: Good. Let's talk cost ballpark - can you run a quick estimate for the bi-encoder + cross-encoder hybrid at 200 qps and top-5 cross-encoder?
06:12 Jamie Park: Ballpark: hosted bi-encoder embeddings at 200 qps is cheap relative to cross-encoder. Cross-encoder at 1000 inferences/sec would be the main driver. For a hosted plan you're looking at X per hour - we'll send detailed numbers, but rough monthly for 200 qps sustained would be in the low tens of thousands, variable by model size and whether you run cross-encoder on GPU. Dedicated commitments reduce per-inference cost by 40-60%.
06:36 Maya Rodriguez: Ok we'll expect a detailed calc.
06:39 Samir Patel: For benching, we'll provide a script that runs realistic query workloads, measures p50/p95, and validates hybrid scoring. We can run against your Milvus endpoints or our hosted index.
06:50 Liam Chen: That script would help. We'll also need to test throughput for concurrent users and cold-cache scenarios.
06:58 Samir Patel: Yes - we recommend testing cold KV cache and warm runs. KV cache matters if you're using decoder-style cross-attention, but for rerank it's mostly index warm-up. We'll document it.
07:11 Maya Rodriguez: Any gotchas when integrating with Milvus versions? We are on Milvus 2.3.
07:18 Samir Patel: We test against common Milvus versions; 2.3 is supported but some index configs changed across versions. We'll include compatibility notes. Also note that vector quantization options (OPQ, PQ) differ and impact recall - we'll list recommended configs.
07:32 Priya Nair: Can Redwood run periodic re-embedding if we retrain models?
07:35 Jamie Park: Yes - we can schedule re-embedding jobs and incremental updates. For Dedicated/Private you control scheduling. For hosted we can run it as a managed job with audit logs.
07:46 Maya Rodriguez: Great. One more question - latency SLOs. You mentioned p50 under 100ms, what about p95?
07:53 Samir Patel: p95 will be higher - many customers get p95 under 300ms with a bi-encoder + small cross-encoder pattern; reaching p95 under 150ms typically requires heavier investment in Dedicated capacity and aggressive caching. We'll include examples.
08:06 Liam Chen: For our user SLA we need p95 under 300ms so that aligns.
08:10 Jamie Park: Perfect. Any blockers for a POC?
08:13 Maya Rodriguez: Main blockers: security questionnaire, pricing, and getting the sample dataset ready. Also need to confirm timeline - target pilot next month.
08:22 Jamie Park: We can do that. To recap next steps - we'll send pricing, security docs, benchmark guide and a sample embedding script; Samir will help set up the pilot and run initial bench. You (Liam) to share sample data.
08:34 Priya Nair: Sounds good.
08:36 Jamie Park: Quick question on sample data size - what is realistic for the pilot?
08:39 Liam Chen: 5k documents with current schema, two months of traffic pattern replay for queries.
08:45 Samir Patel: Perfect. We'll outline the required format in the benchmark guide.
08:49 Maya Rodriguez: Will you also show examples of tuning Milvus efSearch and index params?
08:53 Samir Patel: Yes, example configs and expected p50/p95 tradeoffs will be included.
08:58 Jamie Park: Any other questions from Ventus?
09:01 Priya Nair: No, just timeline - we'd like pilot kickoff by 2026-08-17 if possible.
09:06 Jamie Park: We can aim for that, contingent on documents and data.
09:10 Liam Chen: One small thing - our legal team will likely ask about data deletion and vendor access for the POC.
09:16 Jamie Park: We support data deletion APIs and can provide access logs. We'll include deletion process in the security pack.
09:24 Maya Rodriguez: Thank you.
09:26 Jamie Park: Ok, thanks everyone - we'll follow up via email with the attachments and proposed schedule.

(End of meeting)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional transcription errors, speaker overlap, some product names mis-transcribed (e.g., "Wee-vate" for Weaviate). Audio was clear overall.
